# BickGraphing Code of Conduct

## Our community

BickGraphing is a small open-source tool maintained by the Bick Lab at UW–Madison. It is used by researchers, students, farmers, field technicians, and anyone else who needs to look at a `.wav` file in the browser. Many of our users are not professional software developers, and many are encountering bioacoustics research for the first time.

Because of that, we want this project to feel like an approachable lab notebook rather than a gated technical forum. People should be able to ask basic questions, file imperfect bug reports, and propose ideas without worrying that they will be talked down to.

This Code of Conduct describes the behavior we expect from everyone who interacts with the BickGraphing repository, including issues, pull requests, discussions, and any in-person or online conversations tied to the project.

## What we expect

When you participate in BickGraphing, please:

- **Assume good intent.** Most confusion in scientific software comes from missing context, not bad faith. Ask before assuming.
- **Be specific and kind.** When giving feedback on code, data, or writing, comment on the work, not the person. "This loop reads the WAV header twice" is helpful; "this is sloppy" is not.
- **Make space for non-experts.** Spell out acronyms the first time, link to background, and remember that a question about how a spectrogram works is welcome here.
- **Credit the people you build on.** When you reference prior work, contributions from collaborators, or code adapted from other projects, say so plainly in commits, PR descriptions, or comments.
- **Respect the research context.** BickGraphing is part of an active research program in insect bioacoustics. Treat unpublished data, draft results, and field-site information as confidential unless the owner has clearly made them public.

## What is not okay

The following behaviors are not welcome anywhere in this project:

- Personal attacks, insults, or sustained sarcasm directed at contributors or users.
- Harassment of any kind, including unwelcome contact, repeated unwanted attention, or sexualized comments and imagery.
- Discrimination or derogatory remarks based on race, ethnicity, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, disability, age, religion, body size, citizenship status, or socioeconomic background.
- Doxxing or sharing someone's personal information (including field-site locations) without their consent.
- Misrepresenting authorship, fabricating results, or knowingly committing data or code that you do not have the right to redistribute.
- Sustained disruption of issues, pull requests, discussions, or any other project space.

## Scope

This Code of Conduct applies to all BickGraphing project spaces, including the GitHub repository (issues, pull requests, discussions, code review, commit messages), any official chat or email threads, and any conference, workshop, or lab event where someone is participating as a BickGraphing contributor or representative.

It also applies when a person is representing the project in public, for example on social media, in a talk, or in correspondence with collaborators.

## Reporting a concern

If you experience or witness behavior that violates this Code of Conduct, the preferred reporting route is the **Bick Lab website** at <https://bicklab.com>. The contact form there reaches the lab inbox.

If you would rather email directly, you can reach Emily Bick at `ebick [at] wisc.edu`. Replacing `[at]` with `@` reaches a real address; the obfuscation only exists to slow down scrapers crawling this public repository.

When you report something, please include, to whatever extent you are comfortable:

- A description of what happened.
- Where it happened (issue link, PR link, event, etc.).
- Any other context, screenshots, or witnesses you think would help.

Reports will be handled with discretion. We will not share your identity with the person you are reporting without your consent, except where we are legally required to do so.

## How we respond

The BickGraphing maintainers, in coordination with the Bick Lab, will review every report we receive. Depending on the situation, the response may include:

1. A private conversation clarifying the expected behavior.
2. A public correction or note in the relevant thread.
3. A request for an apology or for the contribution to be reworked.
4. A temporary ban from project spaces.
5. A permanent ban from project spaces, in serious or repeated cases.

We will use judgment, not a strict formula. Our goal in every case is to keep BickGraphing a place where someone with a `.wav` file and a research question can show up and be treated with respect.

## A note on disagreements

Honest technical disagreement is not a Code of Conduct issue. Telling someone their pull request needs more tests, that their proposed STFT change is mathematically wrong, or that you would like to take the project in a different direction is fine, and it is part of how scientific software gets better. What matters is that the disagreement stays focused on the work and the science.

## Acknowledgements

This Code of Conduct is original to BickGraphing but is informed by widely used open-source community norms, in particular the [Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/), version 2.1.
